title: Jacob Bekenstein, an Israeli physicist, showed that black holes have entropy, and changed physics

trailer.text: According to HaMichlol, the scientific community at first received the idea dismissively, and Stephen Hawking also dismissed it.
According to JTA, in 1974 Hawking proved Bekenstein's idea, and today this entropy is called Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.

paragraphs.text: Jacob Bekenstein was born in Mexico City.
According to Wald, he was born on 1 May 1947.
According to Wald, in the early 1960s the family moved to the United States, first to Texas and then to New York.
In 1968 he became a U.S. citizen.
According to Wald, Bekenstein did his PhD at Princeton under John Wheeler, and completed it in 1972.

stations.title: A black hole that swallows everything

paragraphs.text: According to Tsvi Piran, before Bekenstein's doctoral thesis, black holes absorbed everything and emitted nothing.
According to Wald, when matter carrying entropy falls into a black hole, the entropy in the universe, as observers outside measure it, decreases.
According to Scientific American, Bekenstein realized that the accepted description of a black hole violated the second law of thermodynamics.
According to Wald, Wheeler was willing to accept a violation of other conservation laws, but a violation of the second law troubled him.
According to Wald, Bekenstein chose the horizon area as representing black hole entropy.
According to Wald, Bekenstein formulated a generalized second law: the sum of the entropy outside black holes and of the black holes themselves never decreases.
According to Princeton Alumni Weekly, this idea was already in his doctoral thesis.
According to Piran, Bekenstein, a PhD student, struggled with many people who did not like the new idea.
Piran recalls a distinguished scientist who dismissed it as “a mere dimensional coincidence.”
Wald, who studied with Bekenstein at Princeton, wrote that he regarded his project as a foolhardy project that was unlikely to lead to anything fruitful.
Hawking initially argued that a black hole cannot radiate energy, and therefore has no entropy.
According to JTA, at a conference in France Hawking angrily confronted Bekenstein.
Bekenstein recounted that he was then just out of his PhD, facing senior people, and asked himself whether he was stupid and they knew the truth.

According to Wald, there was a real problem with the idea: mathematically the black hole had to be assigned a nonzero temperature, and at the time it seemed clear that its temperature was absolute zero.
According to JTA, in 1974 Hawking proved Bekenstein's idea through a complex calculation in quantum theory, and at first kept the calculation secret, afraid to admit his mistake.
According to Wald, Hawking showed that black holes radiate at a finite temperature, because of a quantum process of particle creation.
According to Wald, Hawking's formula for the temperature made it possible to fix the precise number in Bekenstein's entropy formula.
Bekenstein said that he wrote the formula down first, and Hawking found the numerical value of the constant, so that together they arrived at the formula as it is today.
He also said that the radiation was Hawking's work, and that he had no idea how a black hole could radiate.
According to JTA, the entropy is called Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, and the radiation is called Hawking-Bekenstein radiation, or simply Hawking radiation.
According to Princeton Alumni Weekly, Bekenstein's work created the field of black hole thermodynamics, and this field became the foundation of quantum gravity.
According to Wald, the fact that the entropy depends on area and not on volume underlies all modern ideas of holography in theoretical physics.
This limit is known as the Bekenstein bound.

According to a post published on Scientific American's former blog network, which reflects the author's opinion, some of the biggest ideas in theoretical physics in the last 40 years came about thanks to Bekenstein's insights.
According to Rob Myers, the Bekenstein-Hawking formula is today regarded as one of the most remarkable discoveries in fundamental physics.
Between 1972 and 1974 Bekenstein was a postdoc at the University of Texas at Austin.
According to Piran, the move to the young university in Beersheba was another pioneering step of his.
According to Princeton Alumni Weekly, in 1978 he became a full professor, and in 1983 chair of the astrophysics department.
According to Piran, he built his family in Beersheba and lived there for 15 years.
According to Princeton Alumni Weekly, in 1990 he became a professor at the Hebrew University, and three years later head of the theoretical physics department.
According to JTA, he taught at the Hebrew University for 25 years.
According to Wald, Bekenstein received the Rothschild Prize in 1988, the Israel Prize in 2005 and the Wolf Prize in 2012.
He also received the Einstein Prize of the American Physical Society.
According to Hayadan, the Israel Prize committee wrote that Bekenstein was internationally recognized as the father of the thermodynamics of black holes.
According to the Wolf Prize citation, he showed that black holes have a statistical-thermodynamic property called entropy.
According to JTA, some believed he deserved the Nobel Prize.
According to JTA, Hawking said he wanted the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy equation engraved on his tombstone.

In a 2005 interview, Bekenstein said that he now works on other things and that he thinks he is still doing important things, but it takes time for the public, and even for important scientists, to understand what he did.
According to JTA, Bekenstein wore a kippah.
According to HaMichlol, he was a believing Jew who saw a connection between his faith and his scientific work.
Bekenstein said that, as an observant Jew, he wanted to know how nature works.
According to Piran, he was a strict vegetarian on moral grounds.
Wald wrote that Bekenstein was very modest, both as a student and as a winner of the Wolf Prize.
According to Wald, on 16 August 2015 he died of a heart attack in Helsinki, where he was visiting to present a seminar.
According to Princeton Alumni Weekly, he was 68.
According to Piran, he left a wife and three children, all of them scientists.
Wald wrote that his idea, entropy that depends on area, is a profound legacy for theoretical physics.
According to Piran, Bekenstein's entropy bound aroused controversy.
The dispute was conducted in a series of papers in the journal Physical Review, against Bill Unruh and Bob Wald.

claims.text: לפי JTA, בקנשטיין היה בן להורים יהודים-פולנים במקסיקו, היה אזרח ישראלי ולימד באוניברסיטה העברית בירושלים 25 שנה.
claims.quote: Bekenstein, the son of Polish-Jewish parents in Mexico, had Israeli citizenship and later taught at The Hebrew University in Jerusalem for 25 years.

claims.text: לפי JTA, ב-1974 הוקינג הוכיח את רעיונו של בקנשטיין בחישוב מורכב בתורת הקוונטים, ובתחילה שמר את החישוב בסוד מחשש להודות בטעותו.
claims.quote: But in 1974, Hawking proved Bekenstein’s idea through a complicated quantum theory calculation. At first he kept the calculation secret, afraid to admit his mistake.

claims.text: לפי JTA, אנטרופיית החור השחור נקראת אנטרופיית בקנשטיין-הוקינג, ואילו הקרינה נקראת קרינת הוקינג-בקנשטיין או פשוט קרינת הוקינג.
claims.quote: the entropy of a black hole is called Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, but the radiation emitted from a black hole is called Hawking-Bekenstein radiation

claims.text: לפי וולד, בקנשטיין קיבל דוקטורט מפרינסטון ב-1972 בהנחיית ג'ון וילר.
claims.quote: He then attended Princeton University and received his PhD in 1972, under the supervision of John Wheeler.

claims.text: לפי וולד, בקנשטיין קיבל משרת סגל באוניברסיטת בן-גוריון בנגב בבאר שבע ועבר לאוניברסיטה העברית בירושלים ב-1990.
claims.quote: he accepted a faculty position at the Ben-Gurion University of the Negev in Beersheba, Israel. He moved to the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 1990.

claims.text: לפי וולד, בקנשטיין קיבל את פרס רוטשילד 1988, פרס ישראל 2005, פרס וולף 2012 ופרס איינשטיין של האגודה האמריקאית לפיזיקה ב-2015.
claims.quote: Bekenstein received the 1988 Rothschild Prize in Physical Sciences, the 2005 Israel Prize, the 2012 Wolf Prize, and the 2015 Einstein Prize of the American Physical Society.

claims.text: לפי וולד, בקנשטיין נולד ב-1 במאי 1947 במקסיקו סיטי, ומשפחתו עברה לארצות הברית בראשית שנות ה-60, תחילה לטקסס ואחר כך לניו יורק.
claims.quote: Bekenstein was born on 1 May 1947 in Mexico City. His family moved to the US in the early 1960s, first to Texas and then to New York.

claims.text: לפי ציבי פירן, לפני עבודת הדוקטורט של בקנשטיין חורים שחורים בלעו הכול ולא פלטו דבר.
claims.quote: Rarely, very rarely a PhD thesis changes the way we view the world: Jacob Bekenstein’s thesis was one of those. Beforehand black holes absorbed everything and emitted nothing.

claims.text: לפי וולד, אם חומר שנושא אנטרופיה נופל לחור שחור, האנטרופיה הכוללת ביקום כפי שנקבעת על ידי צופים מחוץ לחור השחור קטנה.
claims.quote: If matter containing entropy is dropped into a black hole, the total entropy in the universe as determined by observers outside the black hole decreases.

claims.text: לפי המאמר ב-Scientific American, בקנשטיין הבין שהתיאור המקובל אז של חור שחור הפר את החוק השני של התרמודינמיקה.
claims.quote: Bekenstein realized that the accepted description (at the time) of a black hole violated the second law of thermodynamics.

claims.text: לפי וולד, וילר קיבל את חריגת חוקי שימור הבריון והלפטון, אך לא היה נוח לו עם חריגה דומה של החוק השני של התרמודינמיקה.
claims.quote: However, he was not comfortable with the idea of a similar transcendence of the second law of thermodynamics

claims.text: לפי וולד, בקנשטיין בחר בשטח האופק כמייצג את אנטרופיית החור השחור והסיק שהיא פרופורציונלית הפוך לקבוע פלנק.
claims.quote: He soon settled on horizon area (rather than on some other monotonic function of area) as representing black hole entropy and deduced that the entropy must be inversely proportional to Planck’s constant.

claims.text: לפי וולד, בקנשטיין ניסח חוק שני מוכלל, שלפיו סכום האנטרופיה מחוץ לחורים שחורים ושל החורים השחורים לעולם אינו קטן.
claims.quote: Bekenstein incorporated black hole entropy into a generalized second law—that the sum of the entropy outside black holes plus the newly proposed entropy of black holes must never decrease

claims.text: לפי PAW, עבודת הדוקטורט של בקנשטיין הכילה את עבודתו פורצת הדרך על אנטרופיית חורים שחורים.
claims.quote: Bekenstein’s doctoral dissertation contained his groundbreaking work on black-hole entropy.

claims.text: לפי פירן, בקנשטיין כסטודנט לדוקטורט נאבק בהרבה אנשים שלא אהבו את הרעיון החדש.
claims.quote: Young Jacob, still a PhD student, had to struggle with many who disliked the new concept.

claims.text: פירן נזכר במדען נכבד שביטל את הרעיון כ"צירוף מקרים ממדי בלבד".
claims.quote: I vividly recall a distinguished scientist who dismissed all this as “a mere dimensional coincidence.”

claims.text: וולד, שלמד עם בקנשטיין בפרינסטון, כתב שראה בפרויקט של בקנשטיין פרויקט נואש שלא סביר שיוביל לדבר פורה.
claims.quote: As a fellow student with Bekenstein at Princeton, I regarded the project as foolhardy and highly unlikely to lead to anything fruitful.

claims.text: לפי JTA, הוקינג התנגד וטען שחורים שחורים אינם יכולים לקרון דבר ולכן אין להם טמפרטורה, ובכנס בצרפת הוא התעמת בכעס עם בקנשטיין.
claims.quote: Hawking disagreed, maintaining that black holes could not radiate anything and therefore had no temperature. At a conference in France that year, Hawking gathered a few colleagues and angrily confronted Bekenstein.

claims.text: בקנשטיין סיפר על ההתעמתות מול בכירים: הוא היה רק אחרי הדוקטורט ושאל את עצמו אם הוא טיפש והם יודעים את האמת.
claims.quote: These three were senior people. I was just out of my Ph.D. You worry whether you are just stupid and these guys know the truth,

claims.text: לפי וולד, התרמודינמיקה שהציע בקנשטיין לא הייתה עקבית לחלוטין, כי מתמטית היה צריך לייחס לחור השחור טמפרטורה שאינה אפס, ואילו אז נראה ברור שטמפרטורתו היא אפס מוחלט.
claims.quote: the black hole would need to be assigned a nonzero temperature, but it seemed clear at the time that the physical temperature of a black hole must be absolute zero

claims.text: לפי וולד, הוקינג הראה שבגלל תהליך יצירת חלקיקים קוונטי חורים שחורים קורנים בטמפרטורה סופית.
claims.quote: The final major breakthrough occurred when Hawking showed that as a result of a quantum particle creation process, black holes radiate at a finite temperature.

claims.text: לפי וולד, הנוסחה של הוקינג לטמפרטורת חור שחור אפשרה לקבוע את הגורם המספרי המדויק בנוסחת האנטרופיה של בקנשטיין.
claims.quote: Hawking’s formula for the temperature of a black hole allowed one to fix the precise numerical factor in Bekenstein’s formula for black hole entropy.

claims.text: בקנשטיין אמר שהוא כתב את הנוסחה ראשון והוקינג מצא את ערכו המספרי של הקבוע, כך שיחד מצאו את הנוסחה כפי שהיא היום.
claims.quote: I wrote it down first, Hawking found the numerical value of the constant, so together we found the formula as it is today,

claims.text: בקנשטיין אמר שהקרינה הייתה עבודתו של הוקינג ושלא היה לו מושג איך חור שחור יכול לקרון.
claims.quote: The radiation was really Hawking’s work. I had no idea how a black hole could radiate.

claims.text: לפי PAW, עבודתו של בקנשטיין יצרה את תחום התרמודינמיקה של חורים שחורים, שהפך לבסיס של מדע הכבידה הקוונטית.
claims.quote: initiated the field of black hole thermodynamics, which became the foundation for the science of quantum gravity.

claims.text: לפי וולד, העובדה שאנטרופיית חור שחור פרופורציונלית לשטח ולא לנפח עומדת בבסיס כל הרעיונות המודרניים על הולוגרפיה בפיזיקה תיאורטית.
claims.quote: The fact that black hole entropy is proportional to area rather than volume underlies all modern ideas of “holography” in theoretical physics.

claims.text: לפי המאמר ב-Scientific American, כמה מהרעיונות הגדולים בפיזיקה תיאורטית ב-40 השנים האחרונות נולדו בזכות התובנות של בקנשטיין.

claims.text: לפי מאיירס, נוסחת בקנשטיין-הוקינג נחשבת כיום לאחד הגילויים המופלאים ביותר בפיזיקה יסודית.

claims.quote: Hawking said he wanted the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy equation engraved on his tombstone.
